author: John T. Morse Jr.
claims: The people had paid dearly for the four months of waiting to get rid of Buchanan after they had discredited him and all his ways.
It was easy to believe that leaving Mr. Lincoln to carry on for four months an administration condemned by the people would inflict a mortal injury to the Union cause.
Many persons not wholly satisfied with Mr. Lincoln supported him for the reason that his administration was condemned by the people.
The great majority of people felt implicit faith and intense loyalty towards Mr. Lincoln.
Mr. Lincoln was the people's candidate, and they would not have any other candidate.
The Republican nominating convention was summoned to meet on June 7, 1864.
Opponents of Mr. Lincoln sought to have the Republican nominating convention postponed until September.
William Cullen Bryant favored the postponement of the Republican nominating convention.
Mr. Greeley artfully said that a nomination made so early would expose the Union party to a dangerous and possibly a successful flank movement.
All knew that the postponement of the convention was a flank movement and desired for the chance of some advantage turning up for those who had nothing to lose.
Mr. Lincoln preserved the same attitude from the beginning.
Mr. Lincoln had too much honesty and good sense to pretend not to want what he very much wanted.
No fair enemy could charge Mr. Lincoln with doing any objectionable act to advance his own interests.
Mr. Lincoln declined to give General Schurz leave of absence to make speeches in his behalf.
Mr. Lincoln stated that speaking in the North and fighting in the South at the same time were not possible.
Mr. Lincoln stated that he could not be justified to detail any officer to the political campaign during its continuance and then return him to the army.
